newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis reports strong Q1 sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Novartis reports strong Q1 sales rise.

text.p: Novartis AG said its 1997 first quarter sales rose 22 percent and growth was particularly strong in pharmaceuticals, thanks to a good start in the key U.S. market.
The Swiss pharmaceuticals and life sciences group reported sales of 8.176 billion Swiss francs ($5.6 billion) as compared to 6.683 billion in the comparable 1996 period.
Sales in pharmaceuticals, its largest single business segment, totalled 3.389 billion, representing an increase of 30 percent in Swiss francs and 14 percent in local currencies.
"The sales growth of 14 percent in the pharmaceuticals sector was driven by the performance in the U.S. where sales in the previous year were comparably low," Novartis said in a statement.
Novartis also reiterated its optimistism about its prospects for all of 1997. But said growth was not likely to remain at these relatively lofty levels for the rest of the year.

"We are very confident about the entire year, that means we see strong growth rates. But I have to say that I would not expect that we would see exceptionally high figures throughout the year," Novartis chief financial officer Raymund Breu said in a telephone interview.
Group sales for the period were eight percent higher when computed in local currencies. Novartis said the 22 percent Swiss franc sales increase was due to the strong positive currency effect.
The Swiss franc has weakened substantially against most other major currencies since early 1996.
The group's agribusiness sales were 17 percent higher, or four percent higher on a local currency basis.
Nutrition division sales rose by 18 percent in Swiss francs and by three percent in local currencies.
Novartis reported increases in Swiss franc terms in all divisional categories except Animal Health, where sales declined by eight percent in Swiss francs and by 22 percent on a local currency basis.

Breu said the decline was due to an inventory reduction process at the distributor level taking place in the U.S. since last year. High inventories were being reduced in the group's Program dog flea control product, he said.
Consumer demand for the product had not declined, but ex-factory sales were down as a result of the inventory reduction, Breu said.
Novartis was formed by the merger of Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG. The company said today that it has introduced a new uniform net sales definition.

For comparison purposes, the corresponding 1996 figures have been redefined accordingly and do not include divested business activities, it added. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.47 Swiss Francs)
